topics.name: Phrasal verbs (break out, carry out, look forward to)
Negative to affirmative without change of meaning

options: The match was called of because of rain.
The match was call off because of rain.
The match was called off because of rain.
questions.rule: call off = cancel. Passive: was called off.

options: Joan spoke confidently to the captain.
Joan spoke confident to the captain.
Joan spoke confidence to the captain.
questions.rule: To tell how she spoke, use the adverb: spoke confidently.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: break into = enter a place by force. Break out = start suddenly (a fire, a war).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Before the noun girl we need an adjective: courageous. Courage is a noun.

questions.before: Robert asked the steward where the girl
questions.rule: Reported question after asked: past tense, normal order. The girl is singular: was.

questions.after: tonight, we will play the final tomorrow.
questions.rule: In the unless clause about the future, use the simple present: unless it rains.
carry on with = continue. Please carry on with your work.

chat: How did the Kabaddi team play today?
questions.rule: played how? Use the adverb: successfully.

chat: Will you come for practice this evening?
options: Yes, unless it will rain heavily.
questions.rule: For a future condition, unless takes the simple present: unless it rains.

questions.prompt: Make it affirmative without changing the meaning.
questions.rule: do not remember = forget. With I, use the base form: I forget.

options: Joan said that she is being seventeen.
Joan said that she were seventeen.
Joan said that she was seventeen.
questions.rule: After said, the present is changed to the past: she was seventeen.

options: Unless you are not honest, nobody will trust you.
Unless you will be honest, nobody will trust you.
Unless you are honest, nobody will trust you.
questions.rule: Unless already means if not, so never add not. Use the simple present after it.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Retreated how? Use the adverb hastily (hasty is an adjective).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In look forward to, to is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing: look forward to meeting.

questions.after: in the old market late at night.
questions.rule: break out = start suddenly (a fire, a war, an epidemic).

questions.before: Her brave words were a great
questions.rule: After a great we need a noun: inspiration.
Reported statement: told + person + that + subject + past verb.

chat: Will you come with us to Granny's tomorrow?
options: I will, unless I will have a cricket match.
I will, unless I have a cricket match.
I will, unless I had a cricket match.
questions.rule: Future condition with unless: use the simple present (unless I have).

questions.prompt: Make it affirmative without changing the meaning.
questions.source: He will not be able to stop them.
options: He will be unable to stop them.
He will be not able to stop them.
He will be disable to stop them.
questions.rule: not able = unable. The sentence keeps its meaning but has no 'not'.

questions.source: Robert said to Joan, 'Get out and wait in the yard.'
options: Robert ordered Joan to get out and wait in the yard.
Robert ordered Joan to got out and wait in the yard.
Robert ordered Joan that get out and wait in the yard.
questions.rule: A command becomes ordered + person + to + base verb.

options: Our team ran out from ideas in the second half.
Our team ran out of ideas in the second half.
Our team run out of ideas in the second half yesterday.
questions.rule: run out of = have nothing left. Past tense: ran out of.

options: Nothing can harmful us if we stay together.
Nothing can harm us if we stay together.
Nothing can harmless us if we stay together.
questions.rule: After can we need a verb: harm. Harmful and harmless are adjectives.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Unless + present, then will + base verb in the main clause: will miss.

questions.before: The captain asked Joan how old
questions.rule: In a reported question, use statement order and the past: how old she was.
carry out = do or complete (a duty, an order, a plan).
Main clause + unless + simple present: unless the captain agrees.

chat: What did the teacher tell you?
options: She told me that bring my notebook tomorrow.
She said me to bring my notebook tomorrow.
She told me to bring my notebook tomorrow.
questions.rule: Reported request: told me to + base verb. We say told me, not said me.

chat: Why are you searching through your bag?
options: I am look for my lost pen.
I am looking for my lost pen.
I am looking for my lose pen.
questions.rule: look for = search. Present continuous: am looking for; lost pen (past participle as adjective).

questions.source: If the captain does not help her, Joan cannot reach the Dauphin.
options: Unless the captain does not help her, Joan cannot reach the Dauphin.
Unless the captain helps her, Joan cannot reach the Dauphin.
Unless the captain will help her, Joan cannot reach the Dauphin.
questions.rule: Unless = if not, so drop does not: unless the captain helps her.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Past story: she succeeded. After were so, use an adjective: so inspiring.

options: Joan told Robert that Polly and Jack had promised to come with her.
Joan said Robert that Polly and Jack had promised to come with her.
Joan told Robert that Polly and Jack has promised to come with her.
questions.rule: told + person; have promised becomes had promised in reported speech.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Smiled how? Use the adverb: smiled brightly.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: cut in = interrupt someone who is speaking.

questions.before: Poulengey will take her to Chinon unless the captain
questions.rule: Main clause in the future, unless clause in the simple present: unless the captain stops him.
Present perfect passive of call off: has been called off.

options: He asked me whether had I finished the project.
He asked me whether I had finished the project.
He asked me whether I have finish the project.
questions.rule: Reported yes/no question: whether + subject + verb, tense moved back: I had finished.

chat: Do you think we can beat them in the final?
questions.rule: Play how? Adverb: fearlessly. With we, use play (not plays).

questions.prompt: Make it affirmative without changing the meaning.
questions.source: I shall not want many soldiers.
options: I shall want only a few soldiers.
I shall want only few soldiers.
I shall wants only a few soldiers.
questions.rule: not many = only a few. After shall, use the base verb want.

questions.source: Joan said, 'I have arranged it all.'
options: Joan said that I had arranged it all.
Joan said that she had arrange it all.
Joan said that she had arranged it all.
questions.rule: I becomes she; have arranged becomes had arranged.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: had not + past participle: thrown. Soldiers is plural, past: were.

options: Unless the soldiers believe in themselves, they will keep running away.
Unless the soldiers will believe in themselves, they will keep running away.
Unless the soldiers believed in themselves, they will keep running away.
questions.rule: Future result with will; the unless clause takes the simple present: unless they believe.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: made her + adjective describes her: made her successful.
Have you ever seen...? becomes whether she had ever seen (tense moves back).
Main clause + unless + simple present: unless a miracle happens.

chat: What did your coach say after the match?
options: He said that we had played well and that he is proud of we.
He said that we have played good and that he was proud of us.
He said that we had played well and that he was proud of us.
questions.rule: Tenses move back: had played, was proud. After of, use the object pronoun us.

questions.prompt: Make it affirmative without changing the meaning.
questions.source: There is no one who does not admire Joan.
questions.rule: no one who does not = everyone. Everyone is singular: admires.

questions.source: Robert said to Poulengey, 'Do you take her idea seriously?'
options: Robert asked Poulengey if he took her idea seriously.
Robert asked Poulengey if did he take her idea seriously.
Robert said Poulengey if he took her idea seriously.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: asked + if + subject + past verb (he took).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: will + base verb: save. very + adjective: determined. looked forward to + -ing: freeing.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Tenses move back: she wanted, she had come. With a person after it, use told him, not said him.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: afraid of; refused to give in (to + base verb); carry off a trophy = win it.
